_meta.name: Case typologies and default red-flag checklists
_meta.note: Typology names and the 'casebook' red flags are shared with the RegRadar Academy casebook (docs/data/academy/casebook.json, fictional). 'default' flags are illustrative indicators written for this prototype: configure them for your firm. AMLR Art. 69(5) requires AMLA to issue guidelines on indicators of suspicious activity by 10 July 2027; replace these defaults with them when published.
common: Activity is inconsistent with the customer's profile and expected activity
Customer is unable or unwilling to explain the source of funds
Unusual complexity with no apparent economic or lawful purpose
Adverse media or a law-enforcement enquiry concerns the customer or a counterparty

typologies.label: Structuring / smurfing
typologies.description: Splitting amounts to stay under a threshold or to spread value across accounts, branches or people.

redFlags.text: Amounts consistently below the €10,000 cash reporting threshold
Sharp departure from a fourteen-year behavioural baseline
Deposits split across two branches
Coordinated timing across supposedly unrelated parties
Rapid consolidation into one controlled account
Several transactions just under an internal or external threshold in a short period

typologies.label: Money mule / pass-through
typologies.description: Account used to receive and immediately forward funds that belong to others.

redFlags.text: Pass-through: funds in and straight out, balance returns to zero
Activity wholly inconsistent with a declared student profile
Inbound senders unrelated to each other and to the customer
Two senders already flagged as fraud victims
New account with high-velocity activity soon after opening

typologies.label: Trade-based / value transfer
typologies.description: Invoices, intermediaries or circular flows used to move value under cover of trade.

redFlags.text: Intermediary adds no logistical function: goods bypass it entirely
Invoice pricing materially above market
Counterparty incorporated four months ago
Beneficial ownership of the counterparty not established
Funds return to an account controlled by the same person: circular flow
Undisclosed common ownership between customer and counterparty
Invoiced amounts exceed the company's entire prior-year turnover
No evidence any service was actually delivered
Payment to a party that does not appear in the shipping or commercial documents

typologies.label: Crypto / VASP exposure
typologies.description: Crypto-asset flows with indirect exposure to illicit services or missing travel-rule data.

redFlags.text: Indirect exposure to a sanctioned mixing service
Volumes roughly twenty times the declared activity level
Travel-rule originator information missing on most transfers
Immediate onward transfer to previously unused accounts
Use of privacy-enhancing tools or obfuscation services

typologies.label: PEP / corruption risk
typologies.description: Politically exposed persons, family members and close associates.

redFlags.text: Senior management approval for a PEP relationship was never obtained
Source of wealth is not documented or does not fit the official position
Complex structures obscure a PEP link

typologies.label: Sanctions / name match
typologies.description: Screening hits, evasion patterns and designated-person links.

redFlags.text: Surname matches a designated individual
A partial name match cannot be discounted with the data on file
Altered names or payment references that look designed to avoid screening
Payment routed through a jurisdiction unconnected to the parties

typologies.label: Merchant / transaction laundering
typologies.description: Merchant-acquiring volumes that do not match the declared business.

redFlags.text: Chargeback rate of 11% against a typical retail norm under 1%
Cardholder geography inconsistent with declared Benelux-only sales
Average ticket four times the projected value
Minimal web presence for the volume claimed
Transaction mix inconsistent with the merchant category code

typologies.label: Cash-intensive business / source of funds
typologies.description: Cash volumes or deposits that outrun the documented business or wealth.

redFlags.text: Cash volume 66% above the twelve-month average
Cash deposits with no documented source
Deposit pattern changes sharply without a business reason

typologies.label: Dormant account reactivation
typologies.description: Long-inactive accounts that suddenly receive or send significant sums.

redFlags.text: Account reactivation after long dormancy
Round-sum credit with no stated reason

typologies.label: Unusual high-value transfer
typologies.description: Single large transfers that deviate sharply from the customer's baseline.

redFlags.text: Amount is a large deviation from monthly baseline
Beneficiary newly added shortly before the payment

typologies.label: Fraud / account takeover
typologies.description: Payments that look like fraud against the customer or by the customer.

redFlags.text: Login from a new device or location followed by a change of payee
Payment instructions out of character with the customer's habits
Customer appears to be coached or under pressure while making the payment
Funds moved on immediately after receipt

typologies.label: Other unusual activity
typologies.description: Anything that does not fit another typology.

redFlags.text: Behaviour or pattern the analyst cannot explain with the information held
